learning_outcomes.text: Familiarize students with the main thermal machines and their operation and function in power-generating thermal power plants. Specifically, students will study gas turbines, steam turbines, combined cycles, cogeneration plants, and nuclear power plants, as well as introducing the basic principles of inverse cycles with the vapor compression cycle.
Know and apply the concepts of technical thermodynamics to the design of steam turbines.
Know and apply the concepts of technical thermodynamics to the design of gas turbines.
Know the principles of Cogeneration and its application to Combined Cycles.
Know and apply advanced concepts of technical thermodynamics to the calculation of refrigeration cycles and heat pumps.
Know the combustion technology and the fuels used in thermal machines.
Is able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Thermal Cycles: power cycles and inverse cycles
Steam Turbine Power Plants: Rankine Cycle
Cogeneration and combined cycles. Gas-vapor cycle
Inverse cycles: refrigeration cycle and heat pump
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment consists of two exams. Exam 1 has a weight of 60%, and Exam 2 has a weight of 40%. To pass the course, the average grade of the exams must be 5 or higher, and each individual exam must have a grade of 3.5 or higher. An optional project, consisting of a report and a presentation, can add up to 1 point to the final grade. Grades from continuous assessment exams are not retained for resit exams; the entire subject content is re-evaluated in the ordinary (June) and extraordinary (July) examination periods.
